sources.entry: SRS - A simple, high efficiency and real-time video server, supports RTMP, WebRTC, HLS, HTTP-FLV and SRT. (Source Code) MIT Docker/C++

summary.one_liner: SRS (Simple Realtime Server) is an open-source, MIT-licensed live media server that handles RTMP, WebRTC, HLS, HTTP-FLV, SRT, MPEG-DASH and GB28181 streams.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes SRS as a high-performance real-time media server that accepts and delivers RTMP, WebRTC, HLS, HTTP-FLV, SRT, MPEG-DASH and GB28181 media. It names support for Linux and macOS across several CPU architectures (x86_64, ARMv7, AArch64, Apple M1, RISC-V, LoongArch, MIPS) and a native Windows x64 build. Codecs listed include H.264, H.265, AV1, VP9, AAC, Opus and G.711. The README points to separate documents for features, architecture, performance, ports, HTTP APIs, DVR and transcoding, and it covers a protocol-conversion path between RTMP and WebRTC. Usage is shown with a Docker image, and streaming is demonstrated with FFmpeg or OBS to an rtmp:// URL, with playback in VLC or an HTML5 player.
use_cases: live stream broadcasting from OBS or FFmpeg
converting RTMP to WebRTC or HLS
serving HTTP-FLV or HLS to web players
notable: Supports many protocols in one server: RTMP, WebRTC, HLS, HTTP-FLV, SRT, MPEG-DASH and GB28181
Runs on Linux, macOS and native Windows x64 across many CPU architectures
Official Docker image for quick start
Documents an HTTP API, DVR, clustering and transcoding
Describes itself as AI-driven and offers an AI Agent guide for maintenance
caveats: The README names some features (clustering, transcoding, DVR, WebRTC conversion) only as topics documented elsewhere, so their details are not in this file
The README does not state platform-specific limits beyond the listed architectures
